title: jerrycan design.json
description: The validated design an app is generated from. Module-grouped with nested subroutes (spec §5). Produced by jerrycan_design; consumed by scaffold/generate/gen_tests. Contract v1 adds entity belongs_to (foreign keys), top-level tenancy (tenant-owned entities), top-level jobs, and field unique/index/values; v0 documents remain valid. Contract v2 adds the top-level storage block (design-modeled object buckets); v0/v1 documents remain valid.

base_path.description: App-level mount prefix applied once to every module and bucket mount, e.g. '/v1' serves all routes under /v1. Health (/healthz) and metrics (/metrics) stay unprefixed. Empty, '/', or absent is a no-op. Must be an absolute path (leading '/', no trailing slash or '//').

cors.description: App-level CORS policy, installed via App::cors. Present => cross-origin requests from the listed origins are permitted (preflight OPTIONS answered before routing; actual responses decorated with the CORS headers); absent => same-origin only. The allowed origins are overridable at deploy time via the JERRYCAN_CORS_ORIGINS env var (comma-separated, '*' for any), falling back to this list — so a cross-origin SPA can be re-pointed without regenerating or hand-editing the tool-owned main.rs.

origins.description: Allowed origins: exact scheme://host[:port] strings, or the single marker '*' for any origin (Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *). '*' cannot be combined with explicit origins or with allow_credentials.

methods.description: Methods advertised on preflight (Access-Control-Allow-Methods). Empty or absent => reflect the route's real methods.

headers.description: Request headers allowed on preflight (Access-Control-Allow-Headers), e.g. content-type, authorization. Empty or absent => reflect the request's Access-Control-Request-Headers.

allow_credentials.description: Emit Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true (cookies / Authorization on cross-origin requests). The Fetch spec forbids combining this with '*' origins — validation rejects that pairing.

model.description: A non-'none' model ('session'|'jwt') activates auth-mode generation: it implies the 'auth' dependency, wires the Auth extension, and turns auth_required/required_roles endpoints into guarded handlers (Session/Bearer extractors + require_role).

dependencies.description: App-scoped dependency names. Reserved names: 'db' (SQL storage via jerrycan-db: SQL repos, migrations, Db dependency), 'validate' (OpenAPI document served at /openapi.json), 'auth' (session/JWT guards + the Auth extension; also implied by a non-'none' auth.model), 'observe' (access-log middleware + /healthz and Prometheus /metrics), and 'oauth' (enables the facade 'oauth' feature so handlers can use jerrycan::auth::oauth::{OAuthClient, Provider}; implies 'auth'), and 'storage' (reserved for the storage extension; buckets are declared in the top-level 'storage' block, not here). Other names are stubs the generator reminds you to provide.

tenancy.description: Declares the tenant entity. Entities with a belongs_to aimed at it become tenant-owned: scoped repositories, a Tenant guard on their endpoints, isolation tests, and a membership table '<tenant_snake>_members'.

entity.description: The tenant entity name (must match an entity declared in some module).

member_roles.description: Roles a member may hold in the membership table.

jobs.description: Background jobs the app declares. The execution engine ships in 0.2 (v2.3); contract v1 freezes the shape so designs and generated code can reference jobs now.

name.description: Job name — becomes the generated job fn/type name.

schedule.description: 5-field cron; engine ships in 0.2 (v2.3) — contract v1 freezes the shape.

queue.description: Optional queue name the job runs on.

storage.description: Contract v2: design-modeled object storage. Each bucket mounts guarded endpoints under {base_path}/<name> (upload, list, download, delete, sign); object metadata lives in the storage_objects table; bytes live in the env-configured blob backend (JERRYCAN_STORAGE). Requires the db dependency and an active auth model.

base_path.description: Mount prefix for every bucket: each serves under {base_path}/<name>. Defaults to /storage, keeping bucket routes clear of module mounts. Must be an absolute path (leading '/', no trailing slash or '//').

name.description: Mounts at /<name>; must not collide with a module mount.

visibility.description: public = unauthenticated GET list/download (still metadata-tracked, cache-friendly); private = every endpoint guarded.

owner.description: Owning entity. The tenancy entity makes the bucket tenant-owned (Tenant-guard scoped); any other declared entity stamps the authenticated user id as owner_id. If the owner entity belongs_to the tenancy entity, objects are additionally tenant-isolated.

owner_prefix.description: Store keys as {owner_id}/… and assert the first path segment on every access — the Supabase storage.foldername(name)[1] = auth.uid() pattern, made mechanical. Requires owner.

allowed_mime.description: Content-type allowlist; image/* globs supported. Violation is 415 JC0415.

write_roles.description: Tenant member roles allowed to upload/delete (#132). Empty/absent = any member may write (today's behavior). Only meaningful on a tenant-scoped bucket (owner = the tenancy entity); each entry must be a declared tenancy member_role — otherwise JC0556. A non-write-role member gets 403 on upload/delete; reads (download/list/sign) are unaffected.

realtime.description: Realtime channels (contract v2): row-change subscriptions (scope-filtered by owner/tenant), ephemeral broadcast topics, and presence topics, served over one WebSocket endpoint at /realtime.

changes.description: Entity names whose row changes are subscribable. Requires db + an active auth model; delivery is tenant-filtered when the entity is tenant-owned.

scope.description: Who may join/publish: none = public, auth = any authenticated principal, tenant = tenant members (delivery partitioned per tenant).

mount.description: Mount prefix for this module (under the app for top-level modules, under the parent for subroutes). Defaults to '/' + name. Path parameters in mount prefixes are fully supported: a handler's single Path<T> binds the leaf-most parameter, and tuples address all parameters root→leaf.

dependencies.description: Module-scoped dependency names (factories or values) the generator must stub. The reserved names 'db' and 'validate' only take effect at the top level — declared here they are treated as ordinary stubs.

table.description: Explicit SQL table name, used verbatim. Absent -> the default snake_case(name) with proper English pluralization (EnergySummary -> energy_summaries). Set this to keep a frozen external schema's exact table name.

belongs_to.description: Foreign-key relations to other entities. Each produces a NOT NULL fk column 'snake_case(entity) + "_id"' referencing the target's pk (nullable instead when on_delete is set_null). For a target in the SAME module the column carries a real DDL FOREIGN KEY with the given on_delete policy; for a cross-module target the column is emitted unenforced and indexed (no DDL constraint — the relation is reported in schema.json with "enforced": false, and referential integrity is enforced in handlers).

entity.description: Target entity name; the fk column is derived as snake_case(entity) + "_id" unless `as` overrides it.

as.description: Optional fk-column alias (issue #119): the fk column becomes '{as}_id' instead of snake_case(entity) + "_id". Lets two belongs_to the SAME entity coexist (a ledger Transfer's from_account/to_account, a self-referential Comment's parent) with distinct columns and distinct DDL FOREIGN KEY constraint names. Absent → the default snake_case(entity) + "_id", byte-identical. JC0560 refuses two belongs_to whose fk columns collide, or an '{as}_id' that collides with a declared field or the pk 'id'.

on_delete.description: ON DELETE policy. 'set_null' makes the fk column nullable; 'cascade' deletes dependents; 'restrict' (default) blocks deletion while dependents exist. The policy is emitted as a real DDL ON DELETE clause only for a SAME-module target; for a cross-module target the column is unenforced (reported in schema.json with "enforced": false) and the policy is upheld in handlers rather than by the database.

public_read.description: The public-read/owner-write shape (issue #105). Valid ONLY on an identity-owned, non-tenant entity in an auth design: READS (GET list + detail) become public — unguarded and unscoped, a list returns every owner's rows — while WRITES (POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE) stay owner-scoped and auth_required. JC0549 rejects it on a tenant-owned or non-identity entity, in a no-auth design, and on any public/unguarded write of the entity.

unique.description: Table-level composite UNIQUE constraints (issue #115). Each inner array is one UNIQUE(col, …) over 2 or more columns, emitted as a CREATE UNIQUE INDEX so a 'one row per (a, …)' invariant is a DB constraint — a duplicate (a, …) insert surfaces as 409 JC0409, no racy SELECT-then-INSERT. Each column is a declared FIELD name OR a belongs_to fk column (snake_case(entity) + "_id"). Single-column uniqueness stays field.unique. JC0559 refuses a group with fewer than 2 columns, an unknown column, or a duplicate group (order-insensitive).

values.description: String enums: only valid on type "string"; becomes a CHECK constraint in db mode and Valid<T> validation.

default.description: A server-owned default value. A field with a default is dropped from the generated request DTO / OpenAPI request schema and the happy-path probe body: the client never sends it and the server applies this value. The field stays required NOT-NULL in the entity/table. Must type-check against "type" (and be a member of "values" when present). Lets a design express e.g. confirmed (boolean, default false) or status (enum, default "active"). When the field also declares range/length constraints, the default must satisfy them (JC0552).

min.description: Inclusive integer lower bound (issue #80). Only valid on type "integer"; must not exceed "max"; not allowed on the pk "id" field. Violations are refused at design time with JC0552.

max.description: Inclusive integer upper bound (issue #80). Only valid on type "integer"; not allowed on the pk "id" field. Violations are refused at design time with JC0552.

min_len.description: Inclusive minimum string length in Unicode code points (issue #80). Only valid on type "string" without "values"; must not exceed "max_len"; capped at 4096 (generated fixtures materialize a minimum-length value); not allowed on the pk "id" field. Violations are refused at design time with JC0552.

max_len.description: Inclusive maximum string length in Unicode code points (issue #80). Only valid on type "string" without "values"; 0 on a required field is refused as unfillable; not allowed on the pk "id" field. Violations are refused at design time with JC0552.

write_only.description: Response-hidden output field (issue #112): the field is emitted with #[serde(skip_serializing)] on the generated Model, so it never appears in an API response, while staying accepted on create/update input and stored. OpenAPI marks it writeOnly. A field named "password_hash" is auto-hidden even without this flag (secure-by-default). JC0554 refuses write_only on the pk "id" (the id must be returned).

operation_id.description: Becomes the handler fn name — lint-enforced (spec §5.3).

required_roles.description: Roles (subset of auth.roles) required to call this endpoint. Non-empty implies auth_required.

public.description: Genuinely public endpoints (credential-issuing login/register, public webhooks): exempt from the unguarded-mutation lint (JL0004) and generated 401 tests. Cannot combine with auth_required or required_roles, and rejected on endpoints whose entity is tenant-owned (a public route bypasses the Tenant guard).

probe.description: How the generator probes this endpoint's success. 'auto' (default) emits the happy-path 2xx probe. 'skip' emits an AGENT TODO instead — for an endpoint whose success needs a credential/signature the generator can't synthesize (login, signed webhook, api-key route), so an uncredentialed 2xx probe could never pass and `jerrycan check` could never reach ok:true. Write its credentialed success + rejection tests in your own test file.
